title: Vendor Questionnaire Triage: LLM-powered Template Matching and Account Risk Scoring
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit heterogeneous vendor questionnaires (SOC2, ISO, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA) and expect fast, consistent triage. Current intake is manual and doesn't factor hosting mode, account sensitivity, or questionnaire similarity to existing templates, causing slow TTR and duplicated effort.

Goal: Build an LLM-assisted intake pipeline that automatically matches incoming questionnaires to a template corpus, computes an account-aware risk score (hosting mode, data residency, ARR tier, regulated industry flags), and surfaces a prioritized lane and recommended evidence bundle for fast responder assignment. Deliver a lightweight API for integrations and a minimal console UI for reviewers to accept/override the automated triage.

Success signals: median triage time reduced by >= 60% for high-volume customers; reviewer override rate <= 25% after GA; reduction in duplicated evidence assembly tasks across accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Automated classifier assigns a template match and confidence score for 90% of questionnaires in test set of 1,200 historical items.
Account risk scoring combines hosting mode, data residency, ARR tier, and past security tickets into a single numeric priority (0-100) with documented feature weights.
Console shows suggested evidence bundle and top-3 responder lanes; reviewer can accept, edit priority, or flag for legal review.
API endpoint /intake/v1/triage returns: template_id, template_confidence, priority_score, suggested_evidence_ids, and human_review_required(boolean).
Privacy: model inputs are redacted per PII policy; raw questionnaire PDFs are encrypted at rest and access-controlled; audit log entries created for each triage decision.
Integration: Connects to existing evidence-store and creates a prefilled evidence collection ticket when reviewer accepts suggestion.
Monitoring: Dashboard tracks triage latency, override rate, top templates matched, and priority distribution by account tier.
Legal confirms acceptable model usage and approves LLM prompt templates before GA (security_review_required met).
tasks: PM: final prompt spec + acceptance criteria (Aisha)
Eng: prototype classifier service using fine-tuned embedding + cosine similarity (sprint 1)
Eng: build /intake/v1/triage API and wire to evidence-store (sprint 2)
Eng: implement account risk scoring microservice and feature ingest pipeline (sprint 2)
Design: console UI flows for suggested bundle review and overrides (sprint 1)
SRE: add audit logs, retention, and encryption checks (sprint 2)
Observability: dashboard + SLOs for triage latency and confidence coverage (sprint 3)
Pilot: onboard 3 existing customers with high questionnaire volume (sales to coordinate)
Rollout: staged release with canary 5% accounts then 25% then GA
notes: Design trade-offs: prefer interpretable template matches (top-3 examples + similarity) over opaque LLM-only labels to increase reviewer trust.
Engineering note: start with embeddings + nearest-neighbor for scale; augment with a lightweight reranker LLM to surface suggested answers where template mapping confidence is low.
Privacy note: do not send account-sensitive metadata to external APIs; use internal/private LLM or on-prem inference for PII-heavy content in pilot customers with strict residency.
Data sources: historical questionnaire corpus (1,500 items), prior evidence bundles, account metadata from billing/custdb, past security incidents table.
Fallback policy: if template_confidence < 0.45 or priority_score > 85, auto-escalate to Legal lane with prepopulated context.
Metrics for PM dashboard: triage_time_median, override_rate, template_coverage_pct, evidence_bundle_reuse_rate, escalations_to_legal.
Potential risks: model hallucination when synthesizing suggested answers; mitigate by showing source snippets and requiring reviewer validation for any generated text.
Cross-team dependencies: Evidence-store (ENG-ops), Customer Success for pilot recruitment, Legal for policy signoff, Solutions Engineering for large-customer mapping.
